transcript: For years, Wi-Fi was just about getting faster internet. Now, one Indian company is trying to make it smarter by putting AI inside it. Here's the scoop. We usually blame slow Wi-Fi on the internet, but the problem can actually be what's happening inside your home. Someone's gaming, someone's on a video call, the TV is streaming in the living room, and suddenly everything slows down. But the internet was probably fine. The real fight was happening inside your home, all your devices pulling on the same connection at once, with a few walls in between and the signal barely making it to the next room. That's where ACT SmartWiFi gets interesting. It has an AI brain called ACT Zippy working in the background 24/7. Think of Zippy like a smart traffic cop for your Wi-Fi. It constantly monitors your network, automatically optimizes the connection, manages where your bandwidth goes, and can even fix certain signal issues before you notice them. So instead of walking over to your router every time something goes wrong, your Wi-Fi is basically trying to sort itself out. That's where mesh Wi-Fi comes in. Instead of one router screaming from a corner, the signal spreads across your whole home, so your gaming doesn't have to fight your 4K TV. Your work call doesn't have to fight everyone else's devices, and your smart home devices can stay connected, too. And you can actually see what's happening through the ACT app. You can check your network health, see every connected device on the device map, and get usage insights for individual devices. You can even manage things like device access and set specific time periods when a device can or can't use the Wi-Fi. That's what makes this interesting to me. It's not AI for the sake of AI, it's AI quietly working in the background to give you a better in-home Wi-Fi experience. And the best part? If you're a new or existing ACT Fibernet user, the upgrade is free with no extra installation hassle. Faster, stronger, smarter Wi-Fi powered by AI. I share updates like these in my WhatsApp community, link in bio.
